rows.en: July, A.D. 1999. A giant object fell on South Ataria, a lone Pacific isle.
rows.notes: Recast as a full sentence ending in this row; next row starts 'It was...'. 'South Ataria' without 'Island' to fit 462 px.

rows.en: It was a giant space battleship, built with tech far beyond Earth's science.
rows.notes: Starts a new sentence to match the recast of u0962.

rows.en: The ship brought a technological revolution through OverTechnology,
but it also pointed to an unknown threat from extraterrestrial life.
A.D. 2000. To counter the threat that was sure to come from space,
humanity founded the "U.N. Government," a body above all nations.
However, no small number of factions opposed it,
and they banded together as the Anti-U.N. Forces,
sparking the conflict that would later be called the "Unification Wars."
The long war finally ended in 2007. Meanwhile, the giant battleship
rows.notes: 'choukika' (long-drawn-out) folded into 'The long war'. No A.D.: the row does not start with seireki.

rows.en: was under constant repair, to be reborn as a U.N. Forces battleship.
After so many years of war, the threat from space that had started it all
was all but forgotten, but the fateful hour was drawing near...
A.D. 2040. In search of new places to live, humanity
had sent many large-scale colony fleets out into space.
Numerous planets had been discovered and developed into colony worlds,
and an age had come when many a generation called one of them home.
Drawn into the first interstellar war in history 30 years earlier,
humanity barely escaped extinction by wielding the power of "culture,"
made peace with the Zentradi, and founded the New U.N. Government.
But the end of the war did not simply mean the arrival of peace.
It began with postwar rebuilding, then quelling some Zentradi remnants,
and even to bolstering defenses against unknown threats yet to come.
The New U.N. Forces were still absolutely indispensable,
and the buildup of new fighting strength went on as well...
A.D. 2045. The 37th colony fleet, which had left Earth seven years earlier,
built around Macross 7, the seventh ship of the New Macross class,
carried over a million citizens through space in search of a new planet.
The fleet's commander, who was also captain of the space carrier Battle 7,
was Maximilian Jenius, the genius pilot of Space War I.
Meanwhile, Macross 7's residential City 7 was governed by Mayor Milia,
once feared even within the Zentradi forces as "Milia the Ace."
She was also Max's wife, wed in wartime in the first interstellar marriage.
Led by these two former aces, the Macross 7 fleet sailed on in peace,
but that a battle with the fearsome Varauta Army lay in wait for them
was something not a single person had foreseen...
A.D. 2059, 49 years after the end of humanity's first interstellar war.
The 25th giant colony fleet to set out, the "Macross Frontier,"
was sailing on toward the center of the galaxy.
The living areas inside the ship recreated the same environment as Earth's,
and over 10 million people went about their peaceful daily lives.
But at the end of that tranquil voyage,
a fierce battle against unknown space creatures lay in wait,
and almost none of the citizens had any idea...
With Boddole Zer defeated, the Boddole Zer Main Fleet had lost its core.
The Zentradi, who knew nothing but fighting under orders,
no longer had the strength to take on the Macross and Vrlitwhai's fleet.
The Zentradi forces, for all their overwhelming might,
had been defeated by the power of Lynn Minmay's song.
Thus Space War I ended, and the New U.N. Government was born.
A new foundation was laid for two races to walk the road ahead together.
Earth, all but destroyed, steadily made its way toward recovery.
Yet new problems were bound to arise sooner or later.
Overpopulation. Resource depletion. And contact with unknown threats.
To solve these problems not yet seen, humanity
planned to send colonists far into space, to new worlds beyond Earth.
Having survived a grueling war,
%s and %s, too,
would in time set out on a journey into space...
And so the Macross's rampage under Sharon Apple was brought to a halt.
The incident was classified top secret,
and word never spread beyond a handful of insiders, but
the danger of runaway unmanned fighters and artificial intelligence
rows.notes: Prefill changed: 'it brought the danger...' did not join with the next row 'came to be recognized'.

rows.en: came to be recognized as a serious problem.
In the end, the full-scale introduction of the Ghost was shelved,
and with it, the development of manned fighters would continue.
The near-derailed development competition ended in a win for the YF-19,
which was formally adopted as the VF-19 Excalibur.
Meanwhile, the losing YF-21's capabilities were also highly rated,
and it was later reborn as the advanced VF-22, getting its chance to shine.
rows.notes: Subject 'it' restored: the previous row's grammatical subject is 'capabilities'.

rows.en: And the two who had flown those planes,
rows.notes: Prefill 'And as for the two...' changed so the sentence across u1032-u1035 parses.

rows.en: %s and %s,
rows.notes: Comma added to fit the sentence across rows.

rows.en: would put their experience with the prototypes to use
and join the crew of a ship bound for the far reaches of space...
The war against the Protodeviln, led by the mighty Gepelnitchi,
rows.notes: Prefill was 478 px; 'immensely powerful' compressed to 'mighty'.

rows.en: had come to an end.
Just as in the war against the Zentradi long ago,
it was the power of Basara Nekki and friends' songs that ended the war.
Afterward, Basara kept on thriving as the vocalist of Fire Bomber,
and became a singer whose voice thundered across the galaxy.
